text:
Evan R.: hey team — quick onboarding Q. Starting next Monday in Toronto. 1) My partner is still in BC; can I add them to dental even though their address is in another province? 2) I paid a private dentist in Vancouver and have an itemized CAD receipt showing GST/HST. Do you need the tax line separated or do you reimburse the gross? 3) My start date is the week of a company-observed civic holiday — will that change benefits effective date or PTO prorate?

Priya (People Ops): welcome Evan! :wave: Short answers: (1) yes, dependents can be added even if they live in a different province. We do need proof of relationship and a proof-of-address for the dependent (utility bill, lease, etc.). (2) keep the GST/HST line on the invoice — upload the itemized receipt to the benefits claims portal (https://benefits.redwood.com/claims) and tag it "newhire-dental". We reimburse the amount you actually paid (gross). Benefits records the tax line separately for accounting but you get reimbursed the full paid amount. (3) benefits effective date is your official start date in Workday; company-observed holidays don’t delay coverage. PTO accrual is prorated from start date and we’ll confirm exact days after payroll calculates the period.

Marco (Benefits): adding: since this is an out-of-network provider, please include service codes or a short note from the dentist if available. If you paid a deposit and then a final balance, upload both receipts and any credit notes so we net correctly. For Canadian hires with CAD bank details, we process reimbursements in CAD. If your payroll bank is USD we convert on payment date.

Evan R.: got it. I do have two receipts (deposit + final) and a written treatment note. Will upload. Also — my partner has a BC health card; is that fine?

Priya (People Ops): yes the BC health card is fine as supporting ID for your dependent. If you can, scan both the relationship doc (marriage cert or common-law affidavit) and the health card and attach them to the claim. If the portal rejects the image, email benefits@redwood.com and we’ll upload manually.

Payroll Bot: :memo: Processing note for payroll/AP: Canadian medical/dental reimbursements for employees with CAD bank details are paid via AP in CAD within 7 business days after claim approval. If bank currency mismatch occurs, expect conversion delays.

Marco (Benefits): one policy note — if there are any covered lab services tied to the claim, we may need an itemized breakdown to apply plan-level maximums. That’s rare for routine dental but I mention it for completeness.

Evan R.: thanks everyone — uploaded receipts and relationship docs now. Appreciate the quick help!
